channel.title: Worldview Weekly
channel.description: A weekly global counterweight reading feed: concise, analytical, low-noise, and deliberately broader in perspective than The Economist.

item.title: Risk of a New Age of Financial Repression Is Rising — Financial Times
item.description:
Financial Times · August 29, 2026 · medium

An analysis of the growing temptation for heavily indebted governments to suppress borrowing costs through interventions, regulation or other forms of financial repression rather than fiscal adjustment.

Why it broadens: Connects bond-market stress to institutional credibility and the political distribution of losses between governments, savers and investors.

item.title: Commentary: China Must Bridge Its Growing Economic Divide — Caixin Global
item.description:
Caixin Global · August 28, 2026 · medium

Zhao Wei describes a K-shaped Chinese economy in which export strength and new industries coexist with weak consumption, falling investment and fiscal strain.

Why it broadens: A China-based economic perspective that emphasizes domestic demand and structural divergence rather than viewing China primarily through trade competition with the West.

item.title: Honda, Nissan to Reach Deal on Joint Development of Vehicle Software — Nikkei Asia
item.description:
Nikkei Asia · August 28, 2026 · concise-medium

Honda and Nissan are moving toward joint vehicle-software development as Japanese automakers confront rising software costs and intensifying competition from Chinese EV makers and technology-led rivals.

Why it broadens: Treats the auto transition as an Asian industrial-organization problem, not simply a U.S.-China technology race.

item.title: Leave Europe to the Europeans — Foreign Affairs
item.description:
Foreign Affairs · August 28, 2026 · long

Jennifer Kavanagh and Justin Logan make the realist case for a substantial U.S. military drawdown in Europe and for transferring primary responsibility for continental defense to European governments.

Why it broadens: A serious challenge to the assumption that preserving U.S.-led alliance structures in their current form is necessarily the safest or most sustainable path.

item.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South? — Project Syndicate
item.description:
Project Syndicate · August 27, 2026 · medium

Adekeye Adebajo questions China’s claim to leadership of the Global South, arguing that Beijing often seeks greater influence within the existing international system rather than a fundamentally different order.

Why it broadens: A Pretoria-based perspective that evaluates China neither through Washington’s strategic lens nor Beijing’s own rhetoric.

item.title: How Climate Is Driving New Geostrategy — Financial Times
item.description:
Financial Times · August 24, 2026 · medium

Climate disruption is beginning to alter shipping routes, energy infrastructure and strategic geography, from Arctic navigation to drought-strained trade corridors and power systems.

Why it broadens: Moves climate change from an environmental-policy silo into the realm of geoeconomics, infrastructure and state power.

item.title: Does Computer Science Need Computers? — Quanta Magazine
item.description:
Quanta Magazine · August 28, 2026 · medium

Ben Brubaker examines the relationship between theoretical computer science and physical computing machines, showing how abstract questions about algorithms and computability evolved alongside actual computers.

Why it broadens: A non-news-driven science selection that restores conceptual depth to a technology conversation dominated by products and corporate competition.

item.title: Why the Global Push to Break Free From Big Tech Keeps Falling Short — Rest of World
item.description:
Rest of World · August 26, 2026 · medium

Cecilia Rikap examines attempts by Europe, India, Brazil and China to reduce dependence on dominant U.S. cloud platforms, arguing that most sovereignty strategies leave the underlying concentration of technological control intact.

Why it broadens: Reframes cloud infrastructure as a global political-economy problem rather than a consumer technology market.

item.title: Americans Are Spending Luxury Dollars for Dive-Bar Service — The Atlantic
item.description:
The Atlantic · August 26–27, 2026 · medium-long

Annie Lowrey reports on the administrative “time tax” imposed by complex public-benefit systems, where repeated verification, paperwork and procedural failure consume large amounts of recipients’ time.

Why it broadens: Examines state capacity from the citizen’s lived experience rather than from budgets, statutes or ideological abstractions.

item.title: 我走進中國科技旅遊「藍海」：深圳會迎來WALL-E美麗新世界嗎？ — 端傳媒
item.description:
端傳媒 / Initium Media · 2026年8月17日 · 中長篇

報導走入深圳新興的「科技旅遊」路線，觀察無人機配送、機器人與城市科技基礎設施如何從產業能力變成可以被觀看、體驗與想像的城市文化。

Why it broadens: 從中國城市生活與本地觀察出發，不把中國科技只當作地緣競爭指標，而是看它如何進入普通人的日常與未來想像。

item.title: India’s Data Center Boom Is Leaving the People It Displaces With Nothing — Rest of World
item.description:
Rest of World · August 27, 2026 · concise-medium

Ananya Bhattacharya interviews digital-inclusion advocate Osama Manzar about India’s data-center buildout, focusing on land, water, electricity, tax incentives and the limited participation of affected communities.

Why it broadens: Puts AI infrastructure inside an Indian development and local-governance frame rather than treating compute capacity as an unqualified national asset.

item.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy — Project Syndicate
item.description:
Project Syndicate · August 26, 2026 · medium

Ngaire Woods argues that democratic governments need institutions capable of sustained industrial strategy if they intend to compete in strategically important sectors rather than relying on markets alone to determine productive capacity.

Why it broadens: Offers a state-capacity argument for industrial policy without assuming authoritarian coordination is the necessary model.
